modules.title: Platform Overview
modules.description: Understand Healthcare Data Lab as the control-plane workspace and {'{kehrnel}'} as the execution engine across domains and strategies.

steps.title: Understand separation of concerns
steps.description: Healthcare Data Lab orchestrates team workflows and UX, while {'{kehrnel}'} executes runtime APIs, strategy activations, and data operations.

steps.title: Identify your workspace path
steps.description: Pick your path by section: strategy design, modeling, data factory, querying, APIs, and apps.

sections.title: Purpose
paragraphs: Home is the launch point for the workspace. It summarizes readiness (health checks), highlights recent activity, and provides shortcuts into the main applications.
Healthcare Data Lab is the control-plane UX. {kehrnel} is the execution runtime behind strategy activations and data operations.

sections.title: Platform Architecture
paragraphs: Use this diagram to understand the division of responsibilities: Healthcare Data Lab provides the user experience and orchestration layer; {kehrnel} executes strategies and performs runtime operations.

sections.title: What You Can Do
bullets: Start your journey with guided navigation into Strategy Studio, Data Models, Data Factory, and Query Studio.
Run a Workspace Health snapshot and review recent health runs.
Review recent activity (recent templates and recent queries).
Jump directly to {kehrnel} documentation for runtime concepts and APIs.

terms.definition: Your team or personal space for environments, strategies, models, jobs, queries, and settings.
An operational context (and runtime connection) used when activating strategies and running jobs.
A readiness signal based on health checks that validate core platform and runtime connectivity.

sections.title: Typical Workflow
steps: Confirm Workspace Health is green (or run a health check).
Open Strategy Studio and confirm which strategies are active for your environment.
Import or review model assets in Data Model Catalog.
Generate data in Synthetic Data and validate outcomes in Jobs History.
Draft queries in Query Lab/Builder and save stable versions to Query Library.

sections.title: Purpose
paragraphs: Strategy Studio is where you browse strategies, inspect their contracts, and activate them for a specific environment.
Activations connect a domain strategy to your environment so runtime operations (synthetic generation, query execution, etc.) can be executed through {kehrnel}.

sections.title: What You Can Do
bullets: Browse the {kehrnel} strategy catalog with search and domain filters.
Inspect strategy capabilities, expected configuration schema, and supported operations.
Activate a strategy for the current environment and maintain per-environment config overrides.
Review environment bindings and confirm the active strategy per domain.
Refresh activation state and re-hydrate catalog data from runtime.

terms.definition: A data protocol or standard (for example openEHR, FHIR, Genomics, X12) associated with a strategy.
A runtime implementation that defines how data is stored, indexed, and queried for a domain.
A binding of (environment, domain, strategyId, config) used by runtime operations.

sections.title: Typical Workflow
steps: Select your target domain (or use the domain filter).
Open a strategy and review its summary, capabilities, and config schema.
Activate the strategy for your environment.
Set config overrides if required for your runtime endpoint or data layout.
Move to Synthetic Data or Query Lab to validate behavior end-to-end.

sections.title: Troubleshooting
bullets: If the catalog fails to load, verify the active environment has a valid {kehrnel} connection and re-run Workspace Health.
If activation fails, confirm the strategy supports your selected domain and that required config keys are provided.

modules.description: Deploy and validate strategy configuration safely in your selected workspace environment.

steps.title: Select target strategy
steps.description: Choose the strategy and domain combination to deploy into your active environment.

steps.title: Apply runtime configuration
steps.description: Configure settings and verify runtime binding before activation.

steps.title: Validate activation status

sections.title: Choose Your Build Path
paragraphs: There are multiple ways to extend or create strategies. Pick the smallest path that meets your requirements, then iterate.
bullets: Level 1: Bundles. Extend existing strategies with mappings/enrichment/shortcuts without writing a full custom strategy.
Level 2: Custom Strategy Pack. Implement a full strategy with its own manifest, defaults, and configuration schema.
Level 3: Multi-Domain Strategy Suites. Coordinated packs across domains with shared indexing, cross-domain query patterns, and unified governance.

sections.title: Strategy Pack Structure
paragraphs: A strategy pack is versioned and published as a single unit. The exact layout can vary, but the following pieces are typical:
bullets: manifest.json: Strategy metadata (id/name/version), domain, capabilities, operations, UI hints.
strategy implementation: The plugin/runtime code that performs ingest/query/index operations.
schema.json: Configuration validation (required keys, types, allowed values).
defaults.json: Default config values used when no environment overrides are set.

sections.title: Validation And Safety
bullets: Validate the pack schema and defaults before publishing to prevent broken activations for other users.
After publishing, activate the strategy in Strategy Studio for a test environment before using it broadly.
Use Workspace Health and Sandbox to validate runtime connectivity and basic operations end-to-end.

modules.title: Data Model Catalog
modules.description: Understand what a data model is in the Healthcare Data Lab and learn how to register, inspect, and use model assets across domains.

video.title: Understanding and Using the Data Model Catalog

steps.title: Understand the role of data models
steps.description: Learn how model assets define structure, semantics, and validation rules before any data is ingested.

steps.title: Upload and inspect model assets
steps.description: Register templates or schemas and explore their structure to ensure they match your strategy requirements.

sections.title: What Is a Data Model in This Lab?

content.text: In the Healthcare Data Lab, everything starts with a data model. A data model defines the structure, allowed fields, data types, constraints, and semantic meaning of healthcare information before any data is stored or queried.

If you are a developer, think of a data model as a strongly typed contract for clinical data. It defines what is valid, how it is organized, and which paths can later be used for mapping, validation, and analytics.
Without a model, there is no reliable ingestion, no consistent querying, and no safe analytics. The Data Model Catalog is the semantic registry that makes this possible.
The catalog supports multiple modeling standards, also called domains. Each domain represents a different way of defining healthcare structure.

content.caption: Data Model Catalog with domain tabs and registered assets.

content.text: Typical domains include openEHR templates, FHIR StructureDefinitions, and ContextObject schemas. Switching tabs changes the modeling standard you are working with, but the governance and inspection workflow remains consistent.
As your workspace grows, you may have dozens or hundreds of model assets. The catalog provides search and filtering capabilities to quickly locate the model you need.

content.caption: Search and filtering within the Data Model Catalog.

content.text: You can search by name, sort by creation date, and filter using domain-specific metadata. For openEHR templates, additional facets such as archetypes or composition types may be available.

Models are typically designed outside the Lab and then registered here. For example, openEHR templates are exported as OPT files, while FHIR profiles are uploaded as StructureDefinition JSON documents.

content.caption: Uploading a new model asset into the catalog.

content.text: When you upload a model, the Lab parses its structure and extracts metadata such as node paths, cardinalities, and data types. Once registered, the model becomes available to Mapping Studio, Synthetic Data, and Query tools.
Each model asset can be opened to inspect its internal structure. This allows developers to verify fields, paths, and constraints before building ingestion pipelines or analytics queries.

content.caption: Detailed view of a registered model, including structure and metadata.

content.text: Depending on the domain, you may see hierarchical structure views, mind maps, raw JSON, or analytics configuration panels. This transparency ensures that the model matches your intended use case before data flows through the system.
A common workflow looks like this:

items: Select the modeling domain (for example openEHR or FHIR).
Upload or import the required model assets.
Inspect the structure and confirm fields and paths.
Use the model in Mapping Studio, Synthetic Data generation, or Query Studio.
Define analytics-relevant fields if cross-patient queries are required.

content.text: In this architecture, models always come before data. This model-first approach guarantees consistency, validation, and long-term maintainability.

modules.title: ContextObject Builder

steps.description: Define object structure and references to strategy/domain-relevant fields.

sections.title: Purpose
paragraphs: ContextObject Builder is used to design reusable context definitions that persist clinical situations (episodes, therapy lines, workups) as first-class objects.
This feature is experimental and under active development.

sections.title: What You Can Do
bullets: Search and filter ContextObject definitions by kind/origin/status.
Create new ContextObjects using starter examples or a guided wizard.
Edit node structure (roles, datatypes, occurrences) and maintain consistent references.
Validate and lint definitions before using them in downstream workflows.

terms.definition: A persisted representation of a clinical situation optimized for fast reads and consistent interpretation.
The JSON specification describing the object shape, nodes, and constraints.
Guided creation flow that bootstraps a usable definition from an example or template.

sections.title: Typical Workflow
steps: Create a new ContextObject from an example (or start from scratch).
Edit the structure and roles for the target use case.
Run lint/validation and fix warnings.
Save the definition and use it in relevant strategy or application workflows.

sections.title: Purpose
paragraphs: Synthetic Data generates test datasets against the active environment bindings. It supports different source modes (runtime/kehrnel-governed, Data Lab samples, and imported data).

sections.title: What You Can Do
bullets: Choose a source mode (for example {kehrnel}-governed generation, Data Lab samples, or imported compositions).
Select templates/models to generate against.
Configure patient counts and validation options.
Launch generation jobs and monitor live progress.
Inspect job outcomes and navigate to Jobs History for deeper troubleshooting.

terms.definition: Controls whether generation uses runtime strategies, local sample data, or imported input.
The structures used to shape generated documents.
Controls whether to validate none, a sample, or all generated documents.
The environment strategy link used when generation runs through {kehrnel}.

sections.title: Typical Workflow
steps: Select a source mode.
Pick one or more templates/models.
Set patient count and generation options.
Run generation and monitor progress.
Review results and open Jobs History if errors occur.

modules.title: Mapping Studio
modules.description: Build and test mapping logic from source documents into target model structures.

steps.title: Prepare source and target artifacts
steps.description: Load source examples and target model assets before authoring mappings.

steps.title: Author mapping rules
steps.description: Define deterministic mapping logic; optional AI assistance can accelerate draft creation.

steps.title: Run and validate transformations
steps.description: Execute test transformations and inspect validation outputs iteratively.

sections.title: Purpose
paragraphs: Mapping Studio transforms incoming documents into target model structures using repeatable mapping logic.
It supports document upload, type identification, template association, mapping configuration (YAML), transformation preview, and validation.

sections.title: What You Can Do
bullets: Upload clinical documents (XML/JSON/CSV/TXT/HL7 v2) and group them by identified document type.
Maintain type-to-template associations so similar documents map consistently.
Author or edit YAML mapping definitions and store them for reuse.
Run transformations, preview outputs, and inspect validation results.
Reprocess documents after updating patterns or mappings.

terms.definition: A classification label used to group similar input documents and reuse mappings.
A mapping from a document type to the target template/model used for transformation.
A deterministic mapping definition stored locally via the workspace API.

sections.title: Typical Workflow
steps: Upload input documents.
Confirm or correct document type identification and associations.
Create or update YAML mapping logic.
Run transformation and review preview outputs.
Inspect validation results and iterate until clean.

modules.title: Jobs History
modules.description: Monitor synthetic and mapping execution history with runtime-level observability.

steps.title: Inspect job status and outcomes
steps.description: Track running, completed, and failed jobs to validate operational reliability.

steps.title: Use history for troubleshooting
steps.description: Correlate job logs and output summaries to diagnose configuration issues quickly.

sections.title: Purpose
paragraphs: Jobs History provides observability for synthetic generation and mapping operations. It aggregates running and completed jobs across your active environment bindings.

sections.title: What You Can Do
bullets: Filter jobs by type (synthetic, mapping) and by status (running, completed, warning, failed, canceled).
Expand a job to inspect parameters, target collections, and runtime metadata.
Cancel running jobs (when supported by the runtime).
Use warning signals (for example missing source templates) to correct inputs and rerun.

sections.title: Typical Workflow
steps: After starting a generation/mapping run, open Jobs History to track status.
Expand a failed job to review error codes and messages.
Fix configuration or inputs, then re-run the job from the original app.

sections.title: Typical Workflow

Save it into Query Library with clear name, description, folder, and tags.
Duplicate it to maintain dev/test/prod variants.

sections.title: What You Can Do

Write or load AQL text and validate/parse it.
Preview translations (for example AQL to MQL) when available.
Execute queries and inspect results and errors.
Save validated queries back to Query Library.

sections.title: Typical Workflow
steps: Ensure an environment has a query-enabled strategy binding.
Load a saved query (or write a new one).
Preview translation and confirm the query shape.
Execute and inspect results.
Save stable queries into Query Library.

Use the blocks to select fields and add filters.
Review the generated AQL output and copy it into Query Lab for execution.

paragraphs: Sandbox is a safe, interactive runner for making API calls against your active environment.
It is designed for testing workflows (create EHRs, upload templates, store compositions, execute queries) without leaving the UI.

Run AQL queries to validate the stored data.
